newsitem.title: INDIA: India poised for 10th normal monsoon - govt.
newsitem.headline: India poised for 10th normal monsoon - govt.

text.p: India was poised for the 10th successive normal monsoon with 29 of the 35 meteorological sub-divisions in the country receiving normal to excess rainfall so far, the government said on Monday.

"During the period June 1 to July 31, 1997, 29 out of 35 meteorological sub- divisions, 71 percent of the districts of the country and 80 percent of the country's area received normal to excess rainfall," the government said in a mid- season review of the June-September monsoon.
It said in a statement that the rainfall for the country as a whole was 98 percent of its long term average for the corresponding period.
The statement said good rainfall will continue especially over the central belt of the country.
It said judged by the performance so far a normal monsoon could be expected for the the whole season as predicted by the India Meteorological Department.
"This year the adverse impact of El-Nino, if any, is not yet visible and the monsoon circulation pattern is quite well established and healthy," the statement said.
El Nino warm water currents raises the water temperature off the coast of South America and can disrupt weather patterns worldwide, creating drought in some areas and floods in others.
The statement said scientific analysis of data over the past one hundred years shows that there is no one-to-one correspondence between El Nino and the Indian monsoon rainfall.
It said there were 17 El Nino years since 1901, out of which nine years had deficient monsoon while eight years had good monsoon.
The South west monsoon advanced into southern Kerala state on June 9, a week later than the normal onset of the monsoon.
The statement said the onset of the monsoon over other parts of the country was also delayed by about a week.
It said during the onset phase a low pressure area caused heavy rainfall from June 23 to 26 over western Gujarat state, causing heavy floods.
The statement said between June 26 to 28 heavy rains occurred over West Bengal, Bihar, Orissa and east Uttar Pradesh resulting in floods in West Bengal and Bihar.
